diagnostic_evidence.quote: \left| \int_{[-1,1]^d} g(x) \, d\nu(x) - \sum_{j=1}^{m} w_j g(\xi_j) \right| \leq \tilde{c}_{d,k} \, m^{-k/d} (\log m)^{(d-1)(k/d+1)} \|g\|_{C^k}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof justifies the rate solely by citing Novak's Theorem/Remark 3, which is stated for the Lebesgue measure on $[-1,1]^d$, while the theorem assumes only $f_{\nu_i}\in L^p$, $p>1$. For such general product measures the univariate Clenshaw-Curtis rules only satisfy the interpolatory bound $(1+\Lambda_m)E_{m-1}(g)=O(m^{-k}\log m)\|g\|_{C^k}$ (Lebesgue-constant loss), so the claimed rate $m^{-k/d}(\log m)^{(d-1)(k/d+1)}$ does not follow and is false in general: already for $d=k=1$, a density concentrated near an endpoint of $[-1,1]$ yields error $\asymp m^{-1}\log m$, not $O(m^{-1})$. The claimed extension to general $\nu$ is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: For the standard domain $[-1,1]^d$, the quadrature error for functions $g \in C^k([-1,1]^d)$ satisfies the estimate \eqref{eq:sg_error_estimte_clenshaw_curtis}, see, \cite[Theorem, Remark 3]{Novak1997}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to $f_{\nu_i}\in C^k([a,b])$ (exactly Assumption 1) and apply Novak's estimate to $h=\qoi\circ\Phi\cdot f_\nu\in C^k$; the rate and all downstream uses are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's stated generality ($L^p$ factorized densities) is false/unsupported; the paper's actual use is under Assumption 1 ($f_{\nu_i}\in C^k$, $k\ge3$), where the rate is restored by absorbing $f_\nu$ into the integrand and using Lebesgue weights, so the main theorem's quadrature-error control survives the repair.
issues.title: Quadrature error rate claimed for general product measures beyond the cited Novak theorem
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition (matching the paper's own Assumption 1) repairs the lemma; the conclusion, rate, and the advertised scope of the main result all survive, and no dependent result loses content.

issues.failure_explanation: The Lipschitz property of Lemma lem:lip_constants controls $\|D\tilde v^\theta(z)-Du^\mu(z)\\|$ only for the SAME spatial point $z$. Both proofs bound $\|D\tilde v^\theta(y_\theta)-Du^\mu(y_\mu)\|$ (with $y_\theta=[\Phi_t^\theta]^{-1}(x)\neq y_\mu=[\Phi_t^\mu]^{-1}(x)$) directly by $\sup_y\|D(\tilde v^\theta-u^\mu)(y)\|$, which is false in general. The missing term $\|Du^\mu(y_\theta)-Du^\mu(y_\mu)\|\le\sqrt d\|u^\mu\|_{C^1}\|y_\theta-y_\mu\|$ is controlled by the already-proved ODE stability bound, so the final conclusions ($O(\|\tilde v^\theta-u^\mu\|_{C^1})$ in the model error, proportionality to $\|\theta-\theta'\|$ in the sub-Gaussianity lemma) survive with slightly worse constants. The identical gap occurs independently in the proof of Lemma lem:sub_gaussian.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing term $\operatorname{Lip}(Du^\mu)\\|[\Phi_t^\theta]^{-1}-[\Phi_t^\mu]^{-1}\|$ (resp. $\operatorname{Lip}(D\tilde v^\theta)\\|[\Phi_t^\theta]^{-1}-[\Phi_t^{\theta'}]^{-1}\|$) and bound it via the existing Gronwall estimates; no new lemma and no change of conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The model-error KL bound and the sub-Gaussian proxy are established by an invalid inference; after inserting the missing triangle-inequality term both bounds, the Dudley bound, and the PAC proof are preserved.
issues.title: Lipschitz bound evaluated at mismatched spatial points in the model-error proof
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, routine completion of the estimates using bounds already present in the proofs; every substantive claim, rate, and guarantee survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The applied inequality $|\log|\det J_1|-\log|\det J_2||\le\sum_k\binom dk2^k\|J_1-J_2\|^k$ is false for general matrices: for $d=1$, $J_1=1$, $J_2=0.1$ the left side is $\log 10\approx2.3$ while the right side is $1.8$; even with $\|J_1\|_2,\|J_2\|_2\ge1$ a $2\times2$ diagonal example with entries $(e^{10},e^{-10})$ vs $(e^{10},1)$ violates it. The smallness hypotheses under which the cited Ipsen corollary holds are never verified in any of the three applications (model error, sub-Gaussianity, McDiarmid concentration). The conclusions are recoverable via the standard local Lipschitz bound $|\log|\det J_1|-\log|\det J_2||\le d\max(\|J_1^{-1}\|,\|J_2^{-1}\|)\|J_1-J_2|$ with $\|J^{-1}\|=\|D\Phi\|\le e^{\sqrt d\|\cdot\|_{C^1}}$ already available in the proofs, but this is a replacement argument in three proofs.

failure_location.quote: the determinant sensitivity estimate from~\cite[Cor.~2.14]{ipsen2008} yields \left| \log \left| \det \left({D_x[\Phi^\theta]}^{-1}(x)\right) \right| - \log \left| \det \left({D_x[\Phi^{\mu}]}^{-1}(x)\right) \right| \right| \leq \sum_{k=1}^d \binom{d}{k} 2^k \left\| {D_x[\Phi^\theta]}^{-1}(x) - {D_x[\Phi^{\mu}]}^{-1}(x) \right\|_2^k

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the cited sensitivity inequality by the local Lipschitz estimate for $\log|\det\cdot|$ using the already-derived bounds $\|D\Phi^\theta\|,\|D\Phi^\mu\|\le e^{\sqrt d\|\cdot\|_{C^1}}$; the linear-in-$\|\tilde v^\theta-u^\mu\|_{C^1}$ (resp. $\|\theta-\theta'\|$) conclusions survive.
issues.overall_effect: The log-determinant terms underlying the KL model-error bound, the sub-Gaussian constant $\bar L$, and the McDiarmid constant $D$ are unjustified as written; all three estimates, and hence the PAC theorem, are recoverable with the standard log-det Lipschitz argument at the cost of modified (but same-structured) constants.
issues.title: Determinant log-sensitivity inequality false as applied
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a replacement argument (a new estimate for the log-det terms) in three separate proofs, although it is standard, contained, and preserves every downstream conclusion and rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Inserting \eqref{subg_est_0}, \eqref{subg_est_1} and \eqref{subg_est_2} into \eqref{subg_init_est} we obtain \left| Z_\theta - Z_{\theta'} \right| \leq \bar{L} \cdot \| \theta - \theta' \|_2 = \bar{L} \cdot d_\Theta(\theta, \theta')

issues.failure_explanation: In subg_est_1 the proof replaces $\operatorname{Lip}_0^\Theta\|\theta-\theta'\|_2$ by the uniform bound $\operatorname{Lip}_0^\Theta 2\sqrt q$, so the first summand (the $\log f_\nu$ term) contributes a constant independent of $\|\theta-\theta'\|$ and the final claimed bound $|Z_\theta-Z_{\theta'}|\le\bar L\|\theta-\theta'\|$ does not follow as displayed. Keeping $\|\theta-\theta'\|_2$ in that single step yields exactly the claimed proportionality with the stated $\bar L$ (the $2\sqrt q$ then remains a valid, slightly larger constant).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Do not replace $\|\theta-\theta'\|_2$ by $2\sqrt q$ in subg_est_1; the stated $\bar L$ then remains a valid constant and the proof closes in one line.
issues.overall_effect: The sub-Gaussian conclusion itself is true, but the displayed proof does not establish the required variance-proxy proportionality; the Dudley bound and the PAC proof inherit only this proof gap.
issues.title: Loss of theta-theta' proportionality in the sub-Gaussianity proof
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction in the proof restores the claim with the stated constants; every substantive guarantee survives.

issues.failure_explanation: Two gaps: (i) the step $\int_0^\infty\sqrt{\log N}\,d\varepsilon\le q\int_0^1\sqrt{\log(1+2/u)}\,du$ has the wrong direction; substituting $\varepsilon=\sqrt q\,u$ gives $q\int_0^2\sqrt{\log(1+2/u)}\,du$ (with the integral truncated at the diameter $2\sqrt q$). (ii) The identity $\E[\varepsilon_n^{gen}]=\E[\sup_\theta Z_{\theta,n}]$ drops the absolute value since $\varepsilon_n^{gen}=\sup_\theta|Z_{\theta,n}|$; symmetrization (or applying Dudley to both $\pm Z$) costs a factor 2. The final $O(LW^2\bar L/\sqrt n)$ bound is preserved (correct constant $\approx96$ instead of $48$), which is absorbed in the concentration bound and the final sample-size threshold.

failure_location.quote: \mathbb{E}\left[\varepsilon_{n}^{\mathrm{gen}} \right] = \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{\theta \in \Theta} Z_{\theta,n}\right] \leq \frac{12 \bar{L}}{\sqrt{n}} \int_0^\infty \sqrt{ \log N(\varepsilon, d_\Theta, \mathcal{H}) } \, d\varepsilon \leq \frac{12 \bar{L} q}{\sqrt{n}} \int_0^1 \sqrt{ \log\left(1 + \frac{2}{u} \right) } \, du

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the Dudley integral with the diameter truncation and add the factor 2 from symmetrization; the rate and all downstream conclusions are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The expected-generalization-error bound is correct up to a factor 2; the intermediate integral chain contains an invalid inequality, and the concentration bound's center and the final PAC threshold inherit only the constant change.
issues.title: Dudley proof: backwards integral inequality and missing symmetrization
issues.why_classification: A short recalculation fixes both steps; the advertised rate and every dependent guarantee survive, with only a constant absorbed by later estimates.

issues.failure_explanation: From $\|D[\Phi^\theta]^{-1}(x_j)-D[\Phi^\theta]^{-1}(X_j)\|_2\le r$ with $r=2\sqrt q\operatorname{Lip}_1\sqrt d\,e^{2\sqrt d\sqrt q\operatorname{Lip}_1}$, the sum $\sum_{k=1}^d\binom dk2^kr^k$ is bounded by $(3r)^d$ or $d\cdot d!2^dr^d$, i.e., by $d!2^{2d}d^{d/2+1}(\sqrt q\operatorname{Lip}_1)^d e^{2d\sqrt d\sqrt q\operatorname{Lip}_1}$, which exceeds the stated $d!2^{d+1}\sqrt q^d\operatorname{Lip}_1^d e^{2d\sqrt d\sqrt q\operatorname{Lip}_1}$ by factors exponential in $d$. The stated inequality eq:second_bd_mc_diarm therefore does not follow; the deficit is $d$-dependent only and is absorbed into $c_{d,\kappa,L_\nu}$ in Remark rmk:main_constant_D, so the theorem's conclusion and the final PAC threshold are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $d!2^{d+1}$ by $d!2^{2d}d^{d/2+1}$ (or bound the sum by $(3r)^d$); the corrected constant is absorbed into $c_{d,\kappa,L_\nu}$ with no downstream effect.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant $D$ is too small as displayed, but only by $d$-dependent factors that are absorbed in the subsequent growth estimate; no rate, regime, or guarantee changes.
issues.title: McDiarmid constant D understated by d-dependent factors
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local constant fix whose entire effect is absorbed by a later estimate; all substantive claims survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof decomposes $\KL(\mu\|\Phi^{\hat\theta_n}_*\nu)\\le\varepsilon_n^{model}+\varepsilon_n^{gen}$ via eq:main_thm_emp_error_decomp, but the decomposition the paper itself cites (eq:empirical_error_decomp) is $\KL\le\varepsilon_n^{model}+2\varepsilon_n^{gen}$. The dropped factor 2 propagates to the PAC constants: the correct chain gives the exponent $-\frac{n}{D^2}\frac{\varepsilon^4}{16384\|\qoi\|_\infty^4}$ instead of the claimed $\frac{\varepsilon^4}{4096\|\qoi\|_\infty^4}$ (equivalently, the tolerances must be halved). The learnability conclusion is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use $\varepsilon_n^{model}+2\varepsilon_n^{gen}$ as in eq:empirical_error_decomp and adjust the tolerances (e.g., require $\varepsilon_n^{gen}>\varepsilon^2/(32\|\qoi\|_\infty^2)$); the conclusion is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the explicit constants in the PAC exponent and the sample-size threshold change by a factor 4; the theorem's statement and conclusion are otherwise intact.
issues.title: Main proof uses the KL decomposition without the factor 2
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local constant adjustment in one displayed chain; the central quantifier, the PAC guarantee, and all regimes survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Controlling $\bar L(L_n,W_n)/\sqrt n$ via $\bar L\le c\exp((c_dW_n)^{2^{2L_n+3}})$ requires $(c_dW_n)^{2^{2L_n+3}}\le\beta\log n$, i.e., $2^{2L_n+3}\le\log_{c_dW_n}\log n^\beta$. But the stated $L_n=\lfloor\frac12\log_{c_dW_n}\log(n^\beta)-3\rfloor$ only yields $2L_n+6\le\log_{c_dW_n}\log n^\beta$; since $2^{2L_n+3}$ grows exponentially in $2L_n+3$ while the right side grows only linearly, the needed inequality fails for all large $n$ (e.g., $2^{2L_n+3}\approx(\log n^\beta)^{1/\log_2(c_dW_n)}$, which dominates $\log_{c_dW_n}\log n^\beta\approx\log\log n/\log\log\log n$). Hence the displayed estimate eq:main_thm_bar_L_est is unjustified and the PAC proof breaks for the advertised schedule. A corrected schedule, e.g., $L_n=\lfloor\frac12\log_2\log_{c_dW_n}\log(n^\beta)-3\rfloor$, gives $2^{2L_n+3}\le\frac12\log_{c_dW_n}\log n^\beta$ and hence $(c_dW_n)^{2^{2L_n+3}}\le(\log n^\beta)^{1/2}\le n^\beta$, and the remainder of the proof goes through unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $L_n$ by $\lfloor\frac12\log_2\log_{c_dW_n}\log(n^\beta)-3\rfloor$ (equivalently any schedule with $2^{2L_n+3}\log(c_dW_n)\\le\log\log n^\beta$); the proof's limit computations and threshold derivations then apply verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the main theorem's proof does not establish PAC learnability for the stated architecture schedule; with the corrected $L_n$ the full conclusion (PAC learnability, adaptive capacity, all thresholds) survives, but the advertised capacity schedule in the theorem's hypothesis must be changed.
issues.title: Architecture schedule L_n incompatible with the key generalization-error estimate
issues.why_classification: The central estimate of the paper's main theorem fails for the stated schedule, and the repair is a reoptimization of the advertised capacity schedule (a premise change), though it needs no new proof architecture and loses no substantive guarantee.
